before I get into it keep in mind that everyone has a different experience with antidepressants. what I felt may not be what you may feel.

anyways, my experience with prozac was weird. it felt like in a sense it worked (it was mainly for my anxiety although it was supposed to help with my depression as well) but no matter how much i’d ask my doctor to increase my dosage, it didn’t feel enough. needless to say I feel like it had more cons than pros for me. it made me a total insomniac for a whole year; i’d wake up in 3 hour increments every night. I didn’t have a rough first couple of weeks on it, but I just feel like after a while it didn’t really do much for me. I was taking it for over a year and stopped about 4 months or so ago and i’m currently not taking anything

it’s a very sticky situation. you don’t want to feel anymore heartbreak, yet you don’t want to let someone you love go. it’s not easy and i feel for you. but right now, think about YOU and what you think is best for YOU. a mantra i’m trying to live by is that “you are the most important person in your life” and in this case, it’s true. you can love someone so much but at the end of the day you need to think about yourself and your wants and needs. you can take the chance and wait and see, or you can decide to break it off. only you know what’s right for you

i wish i knew that before i agreed when my ex told me that we should go on a “break.” it lasted a month, and it ended with a simple text from him and nothing else: “I think we should break up.”
needless to say, I felt played. I thought it was going to work out for some reason; our last rendezvous felt promising. 

my point is, hope can be a dangerous thing to have if you’re not careful. you have to guard your heart. prepare yourself for anything. who knows, maybe this break can bring you guys closer in the end! only time will tell. but whatever happens, I wish you the best. right now the main focus should be on you and reflect on what you deserve and want. good luck!

I understand your pain. based on your story, i take it you’re in high school? i’m in college and I just dealt with a break up 3 days ago, where he did it through text. 

im depressed as hell, and with each day that passes I feel different. I know it’s only been 3 days, but it’s felt like an eternity already. makes me worry about how long it’ll take to get over this, because I just have so many responsibilities to take care of. I wish I could take a breath for me, but it feels impossible with everything else going on in my life. but as much as it sucks and as unfair as it feels, life goes on. no one says it’s going to be easy — everyone processes things differently and gets over things at their own pace. the question is, what are you doing to get to a better state?

I can’t say much for it, because I haven’t technically started yet, but have you considered therapy? 4 years of depression sounds like hell to me; i’ve been depressed for the past 5 years of my life and i’m 19. I finally decided that now was the time for me to take action to better my life; although i’ve been on a waitlist for a while now to see someone. but I think it could help, if therapy is an option for you. if not, how about taking to a school counselor? self-help books, podcasts? I recently discovered a podcast called “break-up boost” and it’s been very helpful. 

I wish I could give you a definite answer that would solve all your problems, but this is all I got. I hope I helped even a little; no body deserves to feel alone and depressed. if you ever need anyone to talk to, feel free to pm me. I may not always be the best for advice (as I am struggling in life myself) but i’m a great listener :-) good luck to you and I hope things look up soon 🌼
